title: Garage width as a proportion of frontage
text: A garage door and its supporting structures (or a garage wall where a garage is aligned parallel to the street) facing the primary street is not to occupy more than 50 per cent of the frontage at the setback line as viewed from the street. This may be increased up to 60 per cent where an upper floor balcony extends for more than half the width of the garage and its supporting structures (or a garage wall where a garage is aligned parallel to the street) and the entrance to the dwelling is clearly visible from the primary street (refer Figure 3.6a).

exceptions.label: upper floor or balcony over more than half the garage width and entrance clearly visible

source.file: Residential Design Codes Chapter 3 - Grouped Dwellings.pdf

notes: Same as Chapter 2 C3.6.3 (50% / 60% limits). Frontage is measured at the primary street setback line. Figure 3.6a: 6 m garage on 12 m frontage = 50%; on 10 m = 60%. Part C C3.6.3 (porch minimum 1.2 m) deleted.

verified.note: Page internally inconsistent: the clause reads 'an upper floor balcony extends for more than half the width of the garage' while Figure 3.6a reads 'upper floor or balcony'. Encoded on the figure reading (parking.garage.upper_floor_over_half_width). Values 50% / 60% confirmed.
